title: Simple Open-Vocabulary Object Detection with Vision Transformers
layout_note: Two training stages side by side, each in its own rounded light-grey-outlined frame with a large title above it ('Image-level contrastive pre-training', 'Transfer to open-vocabulary detection'); the right frame reuses the left frame's two encoders in the same positions and adds detection heads.
grouping: Each stage is one rounded rectangle with a thin grey outline. Within a frame the text encoder sits above the vision encoder; inputs (quoted text strings, a patch-gridded photo) enter from the left. A small legend at the top right of the right frame names the two embedding colours (green: object image embeddings, white: object box embeddings).
shapes_depth: Encoders are large light-grey rounded boxes with dark text; added heads are orange rounded boxes, the two on the right rotated 90 degrees ('Linear projection', 'MLP head') and placed vertically next to the vision encoder's output tokens (small pink tabs on its right edge). Embeddings are small squares: lilac for text, green for image. Text inputs are typewriter-font quoted strings, each word in its own colour on the right. Contrastive loss is a small grid of +/- signs (green plus on the diagonal); detection outputs are rows of probability numbers (bold for the largest) followed by the matched quoted class string, and rows of box tuples (x, y, w, h) in typewriter font. Loss notes are bold-italic phrases ending in 'image' or 'batch'.
proposed_highlight: The additions for detection are the only orange elements, and the text embeddings become a row of 'Query embeddings' across the top of the class-score table; the closing phrases contrast the two objectives in bold italic ('over images in a batch' vs 'over objects in an image').
lesson: Make open-vocabulary detection readable by turning text embeddings into the column headers of a per-box score table, printing the actual scores and the chosen class string in each row next to a parallel row of (x, y, w, h) box tuples.
notes: Venue and year from the arXiv comment ('ECCV 2022 camera-ready version'). The model is usually called OWL-ViT; the figure itself does not name it. Images are photo thumbnails with a white patch grid.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: two framed panels side by side, contrastive image-level pre-training then open-vocabulary detection transfer, with the text and vision encoders redrawn in the same positions so the added heads and changed objective stand out

relations.form: two rounded grey frames left to right, each titled above, the second reusing the identical Text Transformer encoder above Vision Transformer encoder
left panel: the text embedding feeds the columns and the image embedding the rows of a small +/- matrix, labelled 'contrastive loss over images in a batch'
right panel: lilac query embeddings form the columns of a score table whose rows are per-token green object image embeddings, with predicted class labels at each row's end
in the right panel each vision output token fans to both a rotated 'Linear projection' head (class embeddings) and a rotated 'MLP head' (boxes), giving one class row and one box row per token
inputs drawn as data: quoted typewriter strings for text and patch-gridded photos (a bird; giraffes) for images

channels.colour: lilac = text/query embeddings, green = object image embeddings, white = box embeddings (keyed in the right panel's legend), orange = new or pooling heads, grey = encoders; class-name string colours (green/red) mark which query is meant
channels.shape: small squares = embeddings, rounded boxes = encoders/heads, matrix of numbers or +/- = the compared scores
channels.line: grey arrows for all data flow; one long curved arrow per panel points from the predictions to a bold-italic loss note
channels.frame: rounded grey frame = one training stage

quality.strengths: The transfer story is visible by position: identical encoders in identical places in both stages, so the change from a pooled image embedding to per-token heads is the only thing that moves; the compared representations (text and image embeddings) are drawn as squares on the axes of the score matrices; the loss notes contrast 'images in a batch' with 'objects in an image'.
quality.weaknesses: Orange is used both for the pooling+projection block of stage 1 and the two new heads of stage 2 although they play different roles; the per-token fan-out lines from the vision encoder to the two heads converge and cross at the rotated heads; long curved arrows to the loss notes stand in for the loss itself.

insights.structure: Two rounded grey-outlined frames side by side, each titled above ('Image-level contrastive pre-training', 'Transfer to open-vocabulary detection'); in both, a Text Transformer encoder sits above a Vision Transformer encoder in the same position, and the right frame adds two rotated orange heads beside the vision tokens.
insights.data: Text inputs are typewriter-font quoted strings, images are photos with a white patch grid; embeddings are small squares (lilac text, green image, white box); the left loss is a small +/- grid with green plus on the diagonal; detection outputs are rows of printed class scores with the chosen quoted class and rows of (x, y, w, h) tuples.
insights.emphasis: The added detection parts (Linear projection, MLP head, token pooling) are the only orange elements, and the closing bold-italic loss phrases contrast 'images in a batch' with 'objects in an image'.
insights.flow: Each frame reads left to right from inputs through encoders to outputs; in the right frame text query embeddings drop down as column headers of the score table and output rows curve into the set prediction loss note.
insights.avoid: The right frame's many thin curved lines from the pink vision-token tabs to the heads cross and bunch together, and the score digits are tiny.

arrangement.units: two rounded light-grey-outlined frames, one per training stage, each titled in large type above
arrangement.inputs_as: quoted text strings in typewriter font above, patch-gridded photos below, at each frame's left edge
arrangement.losses_at: right end of each frame as a bold-italic text note (and a +/- matrix in the left frame)
arrangement.shared: text and vision encoders redrawn in identical positions in both frames
